corpus.en: The scribe does not send a horse.
The messenger does not send a scroll.
A messenger does not summon the kings.
The messengers do not summon the scribes.
The kings do not send the horses.

accepted: a scribe does not send the scrolls
a scribe did not send the scrolls
a scribe is not sending the scrolls
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. rumha = scribe; husa-su-pa-na = scroll-PL-DEF-ACC; tuwa-ra = send-NEG.

accepted: the scribes do not summon the kings
the scribes did not summon the kings
the scribes are not summoning the kings
toEnglish.explanation: S O V order. rumha-su-pa = scribe-PL-DEF; senke-si-pe-ne = king-PL-DEF-ACC; pete-re = summon-NEG.

toLang.explanation: S V order. tarasa-su-pa = messenger-PL-DEF; tumku = laugh.

toLang.prompt: The kings do not send a messenger.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. senke-si-pe = king-PL-DEF; tarasa-na = messenger-ACC; tuwa-ra = send-NEG.

toLang.prompt: The king does not send the horse.
toLang.explanation: S O V order. senke-pe = king-DEF; tenhiwe-pe-ne = horse-DEF-ACC; tuwa-ra = send-NEG.

grammar: Word order: subject, object, verb. With one participant: subject, verb.
Definite (“the”). A noun without it means “a” (or plain plural).
explain.notes: Vowel harmony: a word's vowels are either all back (a, u) or all front (e, i), and suffix vowels follow the stem. Checked against 320 alternative analyses; the sentences rule out 316, including: -su/-si appears when: (plural or front-vowel stem); -pa/-pe appears when: (definite or front-vowel stem); -pa/-pe appears when: definite & two-participant clause.
